title: QUIZ - 61
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.concept: Translating Rate-Based Word Problems into Systems
questions.learningObjective: Translate a downstream/upstream rate scenario into a system of equations
questions.question: A boat's speed in still water is m and the current's speed is n. Going downstream, the boat travels at 23 km/h; going upstream, it travels at 7 km/h. Write a system of equations for m and n.
questions.explanation: Downstream speed is the boat's speed plus the current: m + n = 23. Upstream speed is the boat's speed minus the current: m - n = 7.
questions.hint: Downstream, the current adds to the boat's speed; upstream, the current subtracts from it.

questions.concept: Setting Up Systems from Word Problems
questions.learningObjective: Translate a two-item purchase scenario into a system of two equations
questions.question: A vendor sells two items: x at $3 each and t at $14 each. A customer buys a total of 8 items for $79. Write a system of equations representing this situation.
questions.explanation: The total number of items gives x + t = 8. The total cost gives 3x + 14t = 79.
questions.hint: One equation should represent the total count, and the other should represent the total cost.

questions.concept: Solving Word-Problem Systems
questions.learningObjective: Solve a two-item purchase word problem by setting up and solving a system of equations
questions.question: Tickets cost $2 for n (adults) and $8 for t (children). A group of 12 people paid a total of $48. How many adult tickets (n) were purchased?
questions.explanation: The system is n + t = 12 and 2n + 8t = 48. Substituting t = 12 - n into the cost equation and solving gives n = 8.
questions.hint: Set up two equations (total people and total cost), then use substitution or elimination to solve.
